introduction: This spec defines the CLI campaign simplification and config restructuring for the `spec` tool — a Python CLI for AI-driven spec authoring. It covers auto-initialization of a default campaign, the new `spec list` command, the `--source` global flag, config path and section changes, and removal of the `spec campaign open` / `new-spec` subcommands.

glossary.AF_SPEC_MODEL: Environment variable that overrides the model selection, taking highest precedence over config file and hardcoded default.
glossary.AgentSpecConfig: Flat dataclass in `agentspec.config` holding resolved configuration fields: `model`, `auth_method`, `vertex_project`, `vertex_region`.
glossary.Campaign.create: Static method in `agentspec.campaign` that creates a new campaign directory and writes `campaign.yaml`.
glossary.Campaign.new_spec: Instance method in `agentspec.campaign` that creates a new spec session, now accepting a `source` parameter.
glossary.Campaign.open: Static method in `agentspec.campaign` that opens an existing campaign from a path.
glossary.Campaign.specs: Instance method in `agentspec.campaign` returning a list of spec directory paths, filtered by `parse_spec_dir_name()`.
glossary.SPEC_DIR: Environment variable that overrides the default spec root directory.
glossary.SpecSession._create: Static private method in `agentspec.session` that initializes a spec session; now accepts a `source` parameter stored as `self._source`.
glossary.ThemeConfig: Pydantic BaseModel in `spec.ui` holding theme/style settings; now always constructed with hardcoded defaults.
glossary._DEFAULT_SPEC_DIR: The Python constant in `packages/spec/spec/cli.py` that holds the default spec root path string.
glossary._session.json: JSON file inside a spec directory that records the current session state.
glossary.auth_method: Config field in `[provider]` specifying the LLM authentication method (e.g. `vertex`, `bedrock`, or empty string).
glossary.campaign.yaml: The YAML file written inside a spec root directory that identifies it as a named campaign.
glossary.context_dir: The working directory used for source code analysis during AI-driven operations (`spec new`, `spec refine`, `spec generate`). Default: current working directory.
glossary.load_config: Function in `agentspec.config` that reads config from `.specs/config.toml` (or `~/.specs/config.toml`) and returns an `AgentSpecConfig` instance.
glossary.load_theme_config: Function in `spec.config` that returns a `ThemeConfig()` with hardcoded defaults only; no longer reads any config file.
glossary.no_session: The sentinel state string emitted by `spec list` when `_session.json` is absent or malformed.
glossary.parse_spec_dir_name: Function in `afspec.discovery` that parses a directory name into a (prefix_int, snake_case_name) tuple, or None if it does not match the spec naming pattern.
glossary.spec naming pattern: The convention for spec directory names: a numeric prefix followed by an underscore and a snake_case name (e.g. `01_my_feature`).
glossary.spec_dir: The resolved spec root directory path used by the CLI, sourced from `--spec-dir`, `SPEC_DIR` env var, or `_DEFAULT_SPEC_DIR`.
glossary.spec_root: The directory where the `spec` CLI looks for and writes specs. New default: `.specs/` relative to the current working directory.
glossary.vertex_project: Config field in `[provider]` specifying the Google Cloud project ID for Vertex AI authentication.
glossary.vertex_region: Config field in `[provider]` specifying the Google Cloud region for Vertex AI authentication.
glossary.\"STANDARD\": The default model tier string, resolving to a standard-capability model.
glossary.\"bedrock\": A valid `auth_method` value indicating AWS Bedrock as the LLM provider.
glossary.\"state\": \"no_session\": JSON key-value pair emitted by `spec list` when a spec has no valid session file.

glossary.--name: Required CLI flag on `spec campaign` for campaign name.
glossary.--path: Required CLI flag on `spec campaign` for the campaign directory path.

user_story.goal: have the CLI default to `.specs/` as the spec root directory
user_story.benefit: so that the new directory convention is used without requiring explicit configuration

acceptance_criteria.action: uses `.specs` as the value of `_DEFAULT_SPEC_DIR` in `packages/spec/spec/cli.py`, replacing the previous value `.spec/specs`
resolves the spec root to `.specs` relative to the current working directory
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a user invokes any `spec` command without passing `--spec-dir` or setting `SPEC_DIR`

acceptance_criteria.action: uses the provided path as the spec root, overriding `_DEFAULT_SPEC_DIR`
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a user passes `--spec-dir <path>` or sets the `SPEC_DIR` environment variable

edge_cases.action: applies the first-found-wins precedence rule (CLI flag takes precedence over env var) and uses the resulting path as the spec root
ignores the `.spec/` directory entirely, emits no warning, and operates on `.specs/` as normal
edge_cases.condition: an old `.spec/` directory exists in the current working directory alongside `.specs/`

user_story.role: developer using the spec CLI for the first time
user_story.goal: run `spec new` without first running `spec campaign create`
user_story.benefit: so that I can create my first spec without understanding campaign management

acceptance_criteria.action: creates the `.specs/` directory, writes a `campaign.yaml` inside it with `name: "default"` and `description: "default campaign"`, then proceeds with spec creation as normal
acceptance_criteria.condition: the `.specs/` directory does not exist in the current working directory

acceptance_criteria.action: skips auto-init entirely and proceeds with spec creation as normal
acceptance_criteria.condition: `.specs/` exists and `campaign.yaml` is present inside it

acceptance_criteria.action: writes `campaign.yaml` with `name: "default"` and `description: "default campaign"` inside `.specs/`, then proceeds with spec creation as normal
ignores the `.spec/` directory, creates or updates `.specs/` and `campaign.yaml` silently, and proceeds with spec creation

edge_cases.action: surfaces a clear permission error message to the user and aborts without proceeding to spec creation
edge_cases.return_contract: exits with a non-zero status code and prints a human-readable permission error message to stderr
edge_cases.error_condition: the `.specs/` directory or `campaign.yaml` cannot be written due to a permission error

edge_cases.action: surfaces the OS-level error message to the user and aborts; no partial state cleanup is attempted
edge_cases.return_contract: exits with a non-zero status code and prints the OS-level error message to stderr
edge_cases.error_condition: writing `.specs/` or `campaign.yaml` fails for any other I/O reason (e.g. disk full, partial write)

edge_cases.action: applies auto-init logic to the custom directory (creates it if absent, writes `campaign.yaml`), then proceeds with spec creation
edge_cases.trigger: a user runs `spec new` with `--spec-dir` pointing to a custom directory
edge_cases.condition: the custom directory does not contain `campaign.yaml`

requirements.title: Global `--source` / `-s` flag for AI context directory

user_story.goal: specify a source code directory for the AI to analyze
user_story.benefit: so that the AI has the correct codebase context when generating or refining specs

acceptance_criteria.action: exposes `--source` / `-s` as a global option of type `click.Path(exists=True)` with a default of `.` (current working directory), stored in `ctx.obj["source"]` as a `Path` object

passes the resolved `Path` from `ctx.obj["source"]` to `Campaign.new_spec` as the `source` parameter, which forwards it to `SpecSession._create`, which stores it as `self._source` on the session for use by `assess`, `refine`, and `generate`
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a user runs `spec new`, `spec refine`, or `spec generate` with `--source <dir>`

acceptance_criteria.action: accepts the flag without error but does not use the value
acceptance_criteria.trigger: a user runs a `spec` command that does not perform AI operations (e.g. `spec list`, `spec campaign`) with `--source <dir>`

edge_cases.action: rejects the argument at parse time using Click's `exists=True` validation
edge_cases.return_contract: exits with a non-zero status code and prints a Click-generated error message indicating the path does not exist
edge_cases.error_condition: the path passed to `--source` does not exist on the filesystem

edge_cases.action: uses `.` (current working directory) as the default source path, stored in `ctx.obj["source"]` as `Path(".")`
edge_cases.trigger: a user runs `spec new` without passing `--source`

requirements.title: Simplify `spec campaign` command — remove `open` and `new-spec`, collapse `create`

user_story.role: developer managing campaigns at non-default locations
user_story.goal: use a simple `spec campaign` command to create a campaign
user_story.benefit: so that the campaign subcommand surface is minimal and unambiguous

acceptance_criteria.action: removes the `open` and `new-spec` actions from the `campaign` command entirely; the `campaign` command no longer accepts an ACTION argument
accepts `--path` / `-p` (required, campaign directory path), `--name` / `-n` (required, campaign name), and `--description` (optional, default empty string) as its only options
calls `Campaign.create(path=Path(path), name=name, description=description)` to create a campaign at the specified path
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: exits with status 0 on success; the campaign directory and `campaign.yaml` are created at the given path

acceptance_criteria.action: treats `--path` as independent of the global `--spec-dir` flag; the two flags do not interact — `--path` governs campaign creation location and `--spec-dir` governs spec resolution for other commands

edge_cases.action: propagates the error raised by `Campaign.create` and exits with a non-zero status
edge_cases.return_contract: exits with a non-zero status code and prints the error message "campaign already exists at <path>" to stderr
edge_cases.error_condition: `campaign.yaml` already exists at the path given to `--path`

edge_cases.action: rejects the invocation as an unrecognized command
edge_cases.return_contract: exits with a non-zero status code and prints a Click-generated usage error to stderr
edge_cases.error_condition: a user invokes `spec campaign open` or `spec campaign new-spec` (legacy subcommands)

edge_cases.action: rejects the invocation due to missing required options
edge_cases.return_contract: exits with a non-zero status code and prints a Click-generated missing option error to stderr
edge_cases.error_condition: a user runs `spec campaign` without providing `--path` or `--name`

requirements.title: New `spec list` command replaces `spec campaign open`

user_story.goal: list all specs in the spec root with their current state
user_story.benefit: so that I can quickly see which specs exist and their progress without opening a campaign

acceptance_criteria.action: scans the `spec_dir` for directories matching the spec naming pattern using `parse_spec_dir_name()` from `afspec.discovery`, reads the `state` field from each spec's `_session.json`, and writes a JSON object to stdout
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: exits with status 0 and prints JSON to stdout: `{"spec_dir": "<relative_path>", "specs": [{"name": "<dir_name>", "state": "<state_string>"}]}`

acceptance_criteria.action: returns an empty specs list without error
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: exits with status 0 and prints `{"spec_dir": "<relative_path>", "specs": []}` to stdout
acceptance_criteria.condition: the `spec_dir` does not exist or is empty

acceptance_criteria.action: sets the state for that spec entry to `no_session`
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: exits with status 0; the affected spec entry has `"state": "no_session"` in the JSON output
acceptance_criteria.condition: a spec directory's `_session.json` is absent or contains malformed JSON or is missing the `state` field

acceptance_criteria.action: outputs the `spec_dir` value in the JSON as the relative path as configured (matching what was passed via `--spec-dir` or the default `.specs`), never resolved to an absolute path
silently skips any directory that does not match the spec naming pattern (including `archive/` and arbitrary subdirectories) and any plain files, using `parse_spec_dir_name()` as the filter

edge_cases.action: returns an empty specs list, silently skipping all non-matching entries
edge_cases.return_contract: exits with status 0 and prints `{"spec_dir": "<relative_path>", "specs": []}` to stdout
edge_cases.condition: the `spec_dir` contains only non-matching directories (e.g. `archive/`) and no spec directories

edge_cases.action: treats the session as absent and sets state to `no_session` for that spec entry
edge_cases.return_contract: exits with status 0; the affected spec entry has `"state": "no_session"`

edge_cases.action: treats the session as absent and sets state to `no_session` for that spec entry
edge_cases.return_contract: exits with status 0; the affected spec entry has `"state": "no_session"`
edge_cases.condition: `_session.json` is valid JSON but does not contain a `state` field

edge_cases.action: returns an empty specs list without error, using the custom path string as the `spec_dir` value in the output
edge_cases.return_contract: exits with status 0 and prints `{"spec_dir": "<custom_path>", "specs": []}` to stdout
edge_cases.condition: the custom path does not exist

requirements.title: Config file paths move from `.spec/` to `.specs/`

user_story.goal: place my config file at `.specs/config.toml` (project-local) or `~/.specs/config.toml` (global)
user_story.benefit: so that config is co-located with the new spec root directory

acceptance_criteria.action: searches for config files at `.specs/config.toml` (project-local) and `~/.specs/config.toml` (global), in that order, using first-found-wins precedence
returns an `AgentSpecConfig` instance populated with hardcoded defaults

edge_cases.action: uses `.specs/config.toml` (project-local) and ignores the global file
edge_cases.return_contract: returns an `AgentSpecConfig` populated from the project-local config file

edge_cases.action: does not read the legacy `.spec/config.toml`; returns defaults as if no config file exists
edge_cases.condition: a legacy `.spec/config.toml` exists but no `.specs/config.toml` exists

requirements.title: Config restructured into `[provider]` and `[model]` sections; `[theme]` and `[spec_tool]` removed

user_story.role: developer configuring LLM provider and model selection
user_story.goal: use clearly separated `[provider]` and `[model]` sections in the config file
user_story.benefit: so that authentication settings and model selection are not conflated in a single section

acceptance_criteria.action: reads `model` from the `[model]` section and `auth_method`, `vertex_project`, `vertex_region` from the `[provider]` section of the config TOML file, populating the flat `AgentSpecConfig` dataclass fields
applies model selection precedence: `AF_SPEC_MODEL` environment variable overrides `[model].model` in the config file, which overrides the hardcoded default `"STANDARD"`
constructs and returns `ThemeConfig()` with hardcoded defaults only, without reading any config file or searching any candidate paths
acceptance_criteria.return_contract: returns a `ThemeConfig` instance with all fields set to their hardcoded defaults

acceptance_criteria.action: retains the same flat structure with fields `model`, `auth_method`, `vertex_project`, `vertex_region`; no structural change is made to the dataclass

edge_cases.action: uses the value of `AF_SPEC_MODEL` for the `model` field, ignoring `[model].model`
edge_cases.return_contract: returns an `AgentSpecConfig` with `model` equal to the value of `AF_SPEC_MODEL`
edge_cases.condition: `AF_SPEC_MODEL` is set and `[model].model` is also present in the config file

edge_cases.action: ignores the `[spec_tool]` section and returns an `AgentSpecConfig` with hardcoded defaults (subject to `AF_SPEC_MODEL` override)
edge_cases.condition: the config file contains a `[spec_tool]` section but no `[model]` or `[provider]` sections

edge_cases.action: ignores the `[theme]` section entirely; `load_theme_config` returns hardcoded defaults regardless
edge_cases.condition: the config file contains a `[theme]` section

edge_cases.action: populates `auth_method` as `"bedrock"` and leaves `vertex_project` and `vertex_region` as empty strings; no Bedrock-specific fields are read or required

correctness_properties.title: Auto-init is idempotent when `campaign.yaml` is present
correctness_properties.for_any: invocation of `spec new` when `.specs/` and `campaign.yaml` already exist
correctness_properties.invariant: the existing `campaign.yaml` is not modified and no error is raised

correctness_properties.title: `campaign.yaml` is always present after successful `spec new`
correctness_properties.for_any: successful completion of `spec new` regardless of initial filesystem state
correctness_properties.invariant: `campaign.yaml` exists inside the `spec_dir` after the command completes

correctness_properties.title: `spec list` always exits 0 regardless of spec root state
correctness_properties.for_any: any state of the `spec_dir` (missing, empty, populated, containing non-spec directories)
correctness_properties.invariant: `spec list` exits with status 0 and emits valid JSON to stdout

correctness_properties.title: `spec list` never includes non-spec directories
correctness_properties.for_any: any directory in `spec_dir` whose name does not match the spec naming pattern
correctness_properties.invariant: the directory is absent from the `specs` array in the JSON output

correctness_properties.title: `AF_SPEC_MODEL` always wins over config file model setting
correctness_properties.for_any: any combination of `AF_SPEC_MODEL` value and `[model].model` value in the config file
correctness_properties.invariant: the `model` field of the returned `AgentSpecConfig` equals the value of `AF_SPEC_MODEL` when it is set

correctness_properties.title: `load_theme_config` never reads from the filesystem
correctness_properties.for_any: any filesystem state (config file present or absent, any content)
correctness_properties.invariant: `load_theme_config` returns a `ThemeConfig` with hardcoded defaults and makes no filesystem reads

correctness_properties.title: `spec list` `spec_dir` output is always the configured relative path
correctness_properties.for_any: any value passed via `--spec-dir` or the default `_DEFAULT_SPEC_DIR`
correctness_properties.invariant: the `spec_dir` field in the JSON output equals the path string as configured, never an absolute path

correctness_properties.title: Auto-init does not interfere with legacy `.spec/` directory
correctness_properties.for_any: any invocation of `spec new` when a `.spec/` directory exists alongside `.specs/`
correctness_properties.invariant: the `.spec/` directory is not read, modified, or deleted; no warning is emitted

correctness_properties.title: `--source` default is always current working directory
correctness_properties.for_any: any invocation of an AI-driven command without `--source`
correctness_properties.invariant: `ctx.obj["source"]` is `Path(".")` and is forwarded to `Campaign.new_spec` as the `source` parameter

execution_paths.title: First-time `spec new` with auto-init of default campaign

steps.action: runs `spec new <spec_name>` in a directory with no `.specs/` directory
resolves `spec_dir` to `.specs` (from `_DEFAULT_SPEC_DIR`), checks for `.specs/` directory — not found
creates the `.specs/` directory and writes `campaign.yaml` with `name: "default"` and `description: "default campaign"`
calls `Campaign.open(path=Path(".specs"))` to open the newly created campaign
calls `Campaign.new_spec(spec_name, prd, mode, source=ctx.obj["source"])` to create the spec session
calls `SpecSession._create(spec_dir, mode, source=source)`, which stores `source` as `self._source` on the session
runs `assess()` using `self._source` as the AI context directory, producing an assessment written to the spec directory

execution_paths.title: `spec list` enumerates specs with their session states

steps.action: runs `spec list` (optionally with `--spec-dir <path>`)
resolves `spec_dir` from `--spec-dir`, `SPEC_DIR`, or `_DEFAULT_SPEC_DIR`
checks if `spec_dir` exists; if not, returns `{"spec_dir": "...", "specs": []}` with exit code 0
iterates over entries in `spec_dir`, calling `parse_spec_dir_name()` from `afspec.discovery` on each directory name to filter non-spec entries
for each matching spec directory, reads `_session.json` and extracts the `state` field; sets `no_session` if the file is absent or malformed
writes the JSON result `{"spec_dir": "<relative_path>", "specs": [...]}` to stdout and exits with status 0

execution_paths.title: `spec campaign` creates a campaign at a non-default location

steps.action: runs `spec campaign --path <dir> --name <name> --description <text>`
parses `--path`, `--name`, and `--description` options; validates that `--path` and `--name` are provided
calls `Campaign.create(path=Path(path), name=name, description=description)` from `agentspec.campaign`
creates the campaign directory and writes `campaign.yaml` at the given path; raises an error if `campaign.yaml` already exists
exits with status 0 on success, or prints "campaign already exists at <path>" and exits with a non-zero status on conflict

execution_paths.title: `load_config` resolves model and provider settings from restructured config

steps.action: triggers config loading by calling `load_config()` from `agentspec.config`
searches for config at `.specs/config.toml` then `~/.specs/config.toml`; uses first found
reads `[model].model` from the TOML file (if present)
checks `AF_SPEC_MODEL` environment variable; if set, overrides the config file value
reads `auth_method`, `vertex_project`, `vertex_region` from `[provider]` section
returns a flat `AgentSpecConfig` instance with all resolved field values

execution_paths.title: `spec new` with `--source` flag threads source directory to AI session

steps.action: runs `spec new <spec_name> --source <src_dir>` where `<src_dir>` is an existing directory
validates `--source` path exists (Click `exists=True`), stores it as `Path(<src_dir>)` in `ctx.obj["source"]`
performs auto-init if needed (creates `.specs/` and `campaign.yaml`)
calls `Campaign.new_spec(spec_name, prd, mode, source=ctx.obj["source"])`
calls `SpecSession._create(spec_dir, mode, source=source)`, storing `source` as `self._source`
uses `self._source` as the AI context directory when invoking `assess`, `refine`, and `generate`

error_handling.condition: `.specs/` directory or `campaign.yaml` cannot be written due to a permission error during auto-init
error_handling.behavior: spec CLI surfaces a clear permission error message to stderr and aborts with a non-zero exit code; spec creation does not proceed

error_handling.condition: Writing `.specs/` or `campaign.yaml` fails for any other I/O reason (disk full, partial write) during auto-init
error_handling.behavior: spec CLI surfaces the OS-level error message to stderr and aborts with a non-zero exit code; no partial state cleanup is attempted

error_handling.condition: Path passed to `--source` does not exist on the filesystem
error_handling.behavior: Click rejects the argument at parse time and exits with a non-zero status code, printing a usage error indicating the path does not exist

error_handling.condition: `campaign.yaml` already exists at the path given to `spec campaign --path`
error_handling.behavior: spec CLI propagates the error from `Campaign.create` and exits with a non-zero status code, printing "campaign already exists at <path>" to stderr

error_handling.condition: User invokes `spec campaign open` or `spec campaign new-spec` (removed legacy subcommands)
error_handling.behavior: spec CLI exits with a non-zero status code and prints a Click-generated usage error indicating the subcommand is unrecognized

error_handling.condition: User runs `spec campaign` without providing required `--path` or `--name` options
error_handling.behavior: Click exits with a non-zero status code and prints a missing required option error to stderr
